colony_summary._panel_background_note: #080E17, DATA'S TABLE (doc/briefs/95-palette.png, 'Grundflaeche / Panels'), 13 September 2026, and it is EVERY panel on this screen: colonyplates.render_fills lays it into each cutout that layout.json's `panels` marks true, and colonyempire and the move notice read it too. A colour choice in the project's own palette (decision 34), not a transcription - the original's panels are whatever COLSUM.LBX entry 0 painted. The header and the galaxy inset name their own keys in `panels` and are the only two that differ. Was (8, 11, 20). `nav_background` stood beside this until the same day and nothing on this screen read it; the galaxy map's own `nav_background` is live and stays.
colony_summary._row_name_note: TRANSCRIBED - the scanned colony's name is BRIGHT and the others are dimmed. COLSUM::Draw_Colony_Summary_For_Colony_ calls COLONY::Set_Colony_Font_To_Blue_(2, colony_idx == COLONY::_g_colony_n) (colsum.cpp:554), and that function picks _font_bright_color_array when the flag is set and _font_color_array when it is not (colony.cpp:533-546). THE DRIVER IS THE SCANNED COLONY, _g_colony_n - the same state that fills the description panel (Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_, colsum.cpp:1155) - and NOT a separate hover, so the two cannot be given different sources. A COLOUR AND NOTHING ELSE: no rectangle, no frame; the only Fill_/Line_ calls in colsum.cpp are the scroll thumb (:759-765). THE ORIGINAL'S OWN VALUES, two independent sources agreeing: the arrays are palette indices {245, 253, 252} normal and {244, 133, 132} bright (colony.cpp:139 and :141) with slot [1] the glyph and [0] the shadow, and measured off the original's own framebuffer on natives_autosave the scanned row's ink is (128, 160, 188) = index 133 and every other row's is (108, 104, 140) = index 253. WHAT IS TRANSCRIBED HERE IS THE RELATIONSHIP, NOT THE RGB: this screen draws in the project's own palette (decision 34), so the scanned name keeps the colour the list already had and the dimmed one is that colour at the original's own dim/bright luma ratio, 0.712. Adopting the original's absolute values would put a 109-luma name on an 8,11,20 panel that is darker than the original's, which is a different question from the one being transcribed.
colony_summary._row_fill_note: HD EXTENSION - decision 57, Data's table of 13 September 2026 (doc/briefs/95-palette.png): row_a #0A121E and row_b #111E2E alternate down the list by LIST INDEX (A, B, A, B from the top of the sorted list, so a scroll or a sort never breaks the stripe), and the scanned colony's row is filled row_selected #182B72. THE ORIGINAL HAS NONE OF THIS: the only Fill_/Line_ calls in colsum.cpp are the scroll thumb (:759-765) and its only per-row state is the NAME's colour (Set_Colony_Font_To_Blue_, colsum.cpp:554, see _row_name_note). The selected fill is driven by the SAME variable as that name colour - colonyselect.Selection.colony, the transcription of _g_colony_n - so the fill and the bright name cannot disagree. WHY THERE IS NO row_hover KEY although the table gives a hover colour (#18345A): on this screen the row under the pointer IS the scanned colony, transcribed from colsum.cpp:880-890 (hover moves _g_colony_n), so a hovered row is always the selected row and the selected fill wins - a hover key would be a colour nothing can ever show. Drawn in colonylist.render UNDER the cell outlines. Data's decision (a), 13 September 2026.
colony_summary._plate_outline_note: #29394C, Data's table ('Trennlinien'), 13 September 2026: the 1 px outline around every cell of every band of the colony list (colonylist.render through StyleRenderer.draw_plate, decision 51 - a DEVIATION IN KIND, since the original paints its cell plates into the COLSUM.LBX bitmap). It had no entry here and lived as a code default (55, 65, 85) in colonylist; it has no code default now (palette.require, decision 14). ONLY THE LIST'S CELLS: the header plates are drawn with panel.thin_border, a key every screen shares, and planet_output's own line is output_separator - both unchanged.
colony_summary._header_note: Data's table, 13 September 2026: header background #09111D and header text #79A8E8 (the table says 'ca.'). Colour choices in the project's own palette (decision 34), not transcriptions and not an extension: the header window is ours already (colonyheader, a marked DEVIATION). The background reaches the header cutout through layout.json `panels.header`, which names this key instead of the panel base; the text is the five column words, and `label` - which the scan box, the sidebar and the scroll arrows also read - is untouched.
colony_summary._galaxy_inset_fill_note: BLACK, and it is a measurement rather than a taste. MOVED HERE FROM layout.json's `panels` on 13 September 2026 (brief 96): a colour belongs in the skin, and `panels.galaxy_inset` now names this key. The panel fill this screen lays down elsewhere is panel_background; the ORIGINAL's own inset region measures (0, 8, 0) over 2475 of about 2700 samples in the 640x480 frame at native (380, 349, 128, 91). So the box always had a fill - the cockpit texture was never showing through - and black moves TOWARD the original rather than away from it. It is a per-box fill and not a change to colonyinset, which deliberately draws no background of its own: Draw_Galaxy_Map_Box_ fills black only when _using_colony_screen_palette == 0 (movebox.cpp:36-38) and this screen sets that flag, so the original inherits whatever the screen put there and so do we.
colony_summary._output_separator_note: HD EXTENSION - the line between two rows of planet_output (decision 56, layout.json output._separator_note). The original draws no line in that box, so there is no palette index to transcribe: this is a design value, a dim blue between panel_background (8, 11, 20) and label (128, 146, 180), chosen so the line groups a row without competing with its text. Data's to change on the side-by-side.
colony_summary._slider_note: TRANSCRIBED from COLSUM::Draw_Bar_Indicator_ (colsum.cpp:747-771). The thumb is Fill_(621, y1, 626, y2, 229) with Line_ borders in 230 on the top and left edges and 228 on the bottom and right (:762-765), and the track's four corners are Dot_(...,80) at y 40 and y 311 (:767-770). The palette indices resolved against the game's own live palette on natives_autosave: 229 -> (28,28,164), 230 -> (60,60,212), 228 -> (0,0,108), 80 -> (0,0,0). These are ABSOLUTE values and not a relationship, unlike the name colours above: the slider is a control with no counterpart in this project's palette to keep faith with, and colonyfirst already reads index 229 back off the framebuffer to recover _first - so a different blue here would make the drawing and the reading disagree about what the same thing looks like.

planets._owner_note: The Planets list prints a row in its OWNER's colour and brighter under the pointer - PLNTSUM::Colony_Owner_Colors_ / Player_Colors_ (plntsum.cpp:2204-2252): the planet's colony owner's player colour, the neutral ramp when nobody holds it, and highlight type 1 for the scanned row (Summary_Screen_Print_Data_, plntsum.cpp:62-70). Data's decision (a), brief 101 Stop 1: owner colours and the original's highlights, keyed here; the mockup's scheme is dropped. THE BASE COLOURS ARE NOT REPEATED: an owned row reads galaxy_map.owner_<player colour>, the one home of the eight player colours. What is here is what the galaxy map has no key for - the neutral ramp and the eight hover shades. The original resolves both through Font_Colors2_ against its own palette (base = colour * 6 - 0x31, hover shade +3/+5 against +2/+4), which this project cannot read (the palette-index lesson in colonyinset.py), so the values are this skin's: the owner colour lifted toward white by about a third. Highlight type 2 (the armed send, unreachable) waits with the send brief and has no key yet.
planets._neutral_note: TRANSCRIBED FROM THE PALETTE, brief 101 (Data's answer 4 after Stop 3). An unowned row prints through Colony_Owner_Colors_(-1, 0) -> Player_Colors_(-1, 0) -> MISC::Font_Colors2_(4, 0x40, 0x41) (plntsum.cpp:2204-2232, misc.cpp:71-80): colour slots 1-7 are 0x41 and slot 0 is 0x40. Measured on the native frame of screen 32 on slot 8 (fixture_reference_3502.4.GAM): the neutral climate text of row 1 is 110 px of index 65 (0x41) and 20 of index 64, nothing else. Index 0x41 in the Planets screen's own palette (fonts::Load_Palette_(6, ...), plntsum.cpp:1965) is (104, 128, 124) - the value above, read from the palette the snapshot carries, not from a screenshot by eye. neutral_hover and the owner hover shades are still this skin's values.
planets._status_note: The status line's three colours - Summary_Screen_Print_Scanned_ (plntsum.cpp:1918-1925) picks _red_colors, _green_colors or _hi_neutral_colors by its status 1 / 2 / 0. Values are this skin's, for the same palette reason as above: red for a black hole or a blocked or unreachable system, green for a reachable one (armed send only), neutral for a star name or 'unexplored'.
planets._control_note: The side column's words and fills - the sort keys, the five restrictions, the two send buttons and RETURN. The original draws those as PLNTSUM.LBX sprites with no string behind them; the fills are the colony summary's nav_active / nav_hover values, repeated under this screen's own keys so a skin can tell the two screens apart. control_disabled_text is a send button whose field the game did not add (Add_Plntsum_Fields_, plntsum.cpp:708-718).
